scope: Selected dated ancient, medieval and modern capitals; incomplete, independently sourced from border snapshots. Modern coverage ends at 2025.
temporalPolicy: Inclusive annual windows represent status during a year. Exact event dates are documented in notes; markers do not assert that the change occurred on 1 January. Transition years can overlap. A to value of 2025 is a coverage ceiling, not an end-of-capital event. Older chronologies conservatively omit some uncertain transition years.

periods.label: Federal capital of reunified Germany
periods.note: The 1990 Unification Treaty established Berlin as capital. Parliament and the principal government seat moved in 1999; some federal ministries remain in Bonn. Capital status and government relocation are distinct. The final year 2025 is this dataset’s coverage ceiling, not the end of capital status.

capitals.name: Moscow
capitals.coordinateNote: Reba et al. gazetteer reference point shared with the city dataset; not an exact government building or surveyed historic urban footprint.

periods.label: Russian SFSR capital
periods.note: The Soviet Russian government transferred the capital on 12 March 1918. Moscow remained the RSFSR capital within the Soviet Union; the 1991 state-name transition is represented at annual precision.

periods.label: Soviet Union capital
periods.note: Moscow was capital of the USSR from its formation in 1922 until dissolution in 1991. The same city was also the RSFSR capital. Transition-year overlaps are intentional; this dataset does not assert daily precision.

periods.label: Russian Federation capital
periods.note: Moscow remained the capital through the late-1991 transition from the RSFSR and dissolution of the USSR. The 1991 overlap records status at different points within that year, not simultaneous unchanged states for the whole year. The final year 2025 is this dataset’s coverage ceiling, not the end of capital status.
